Graphical summary of information flow and tools in DE-EE0009664 5 Bradley, T.H., et al., Agent-Based, Bottom-Up Medium- and Heavy-duty Electric Vehicle Economics, Operation, Charging and Adoption, Final Technical Report, DE-EE0009664 This project was able to achieve the DOE’s goals of developing new modeling tools to understand MDHD vehicle operation and adoption. The first modeling tool is a fleet-level techno- economic analysis model capable of estimating energy use and associated environmental and cost impacts for electrified and conventional vehicles of any MDHD vocation, using real-world cost and operations data, including approaches to optimizing schedules for charging and/or vehicle dispatch. The second modeling tool is a system-level, bottom-up, agent-based adoption model capable of generating geographically-resolved estimates of market projections for MDHD vehicles and charging infrastructure. These tools will be developed and to serve dual purposes as analysis tools for researchers, and decision-support tools for decision makers within the MDHD system. Key research contributions from this project include: • This project has improved the set of analytical models that are available to DOE researchers, the academic research community, and commercial customers. The partnerships available in this team enable the integration of rigorous computation tools with informed and novel datasets. Because we have chosen to seek open-source software distribution, fleet operators of all sizes and vocations and other investors in charging infrastructure will now have access to a customizable and scientific tool for assessing suitability, costs, energy usage, and emissions during the design and specification of eMDHD fleets and charging infrastructure. • This project has now improved the set of models that are available for assessing the value of managed charging policies, market models, control systems, and infrastructure investments. DOE Policymakers, utilities, automakers, and other strategic entities will now have access to a highly integrated, bottom-up, agent-based eMDHD adoption modeling tool for assessing the potential effects of technology infusions, policy, changing economics, and the DOE technology/product suite. • Through a novel means of predictive modeling of eMDHD adoption, this proposal shas informed and derisked the development of the infrastructure for eMDHD vehicles. Using a novel ABM framework and the results of the detailed microsimulation results as prerequisites, we now have a new technology for bottom-up adoption modeling of eMDHD vehicles with geographical, application-specific, and temporal resolution. Together, these outcomes have helped DOE and the US to achieve the overarching goals of accelerating the equitable, inclusive, and sustainable transition towards electrification of commercial transport. This material is based upon work supported by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy (EERE).
